scenes.title: Three seats. Same broken process.
bullets: Agency recruiting — watched companies lose time on candidates who looked right on paper but missed culture and team fit.
In-house recruiting & HR — felt the pressure to fill every open seat with the right person, not just the available one.
As a candidate — lived the opacity, uncertainty, and gap between interview theater and day-to-day reality.

scenes.title: Missing transparency. Missing certainty. Missing fit.
scenes.body: Interviews run one way. People interview another way. Then work starts — and the gaps show. Intuition alone is no longer enough.

label: The Problem
tagline: Fit is still hard to understand

scenes.title: Hiring has more data than ever.
scenes.highlight: But fit is still hard to understand.
scenes.body: Despite CVs, LinkedIn, assessments and AI screening — decisions still run on incomplete understanding.

scenes.title: Both sides under pressure

left.title: Candidates
items: Layoffs, AI shifts, and reserve duty pushed strong talent into the market.
Candidates search for ways to stand out beyond the CV.
Low process transparency → frustration and drop-off.

right.title: Companies
items: Headcount is tighter — every open role is critical.
The pressure: fill the seat with the best-fit person, not the fastest one.
A wrong hire costs time, money, and team momentum.

scenes.title: Many candidates move forward — mismatches still happen
scenes.body: CV → Screening → Interview → Intuition → Hire. Thousands at the top. One at the bottom. Still no clear mutual fit signal.

scenes.title: Almost no tools differentiate by deep fit
bullets: Most tools optimize keywords and experience — not company, role, and team fit together.
Recruiters still grind through CV screening, phone screens, onsite loops, and take-homes.
Generic questions fill the first call instead of a conversation that starts from fit and gaps.

scenes.title: It is not finding more candidates.
The match is simple.
scenes.body: mingle is not another AI feature on top of an ATS. It is a new intelligence layer for both sides of the employment relationship.
